Section: Old Testament
Catalogue note: The Church’s English canon list names Genesis; the exact manuscript recension and its mapping to this historical critical edition are edition-specific.
Edition / translation: August Dillmann (ed.), Veteris Testamenti Aethiopici Tomus Primus, sive Octateuchus Aethiopicus, Leipzig, 1853–1855; digitized and transcribed by Ran HaCohen.
Catalogue chapter note: 50 chapters in the digitized edition
Text availability: Complete 50-chapter Geʽez transcription bundled with Brenton’s 50-chapter English Septuagint companion; English is not translated directly from the Geʽez witness. 8 separately scoped Genesis title-candidate research readers across 8 language tags; these are discovery links, not verified Ethiopian or Eritrean Orthodox editions or canon-linked readers. Per-reader source, rights, and review limits remain attached individually.
Completeness: All 50 source chapter pages are present for each bundled witness. The Geʽez transcription has 1,526 linked verse markers; Brenton has 1,532 English labels and retains lettered labels such as 50a. This checks captured source inventory, not manuscript-level textual completeness or full cross-witness alignment.
Rights note: Geʽez: noncommercial copy/distribution only with © Ran HaCohen and permission notice; commercial rights not granted. Brenton English translation: public domain. Separate terms apply.

eotc-088  Ethiopic Clement (Qälementos)
Section: New Testament
Catalogue note: Working research row; candidate for the Church-list Book of Clement, but exact crosswalk remains uncertain because the Church page does not supply the Geʽez title
Edition / translation: Bausi (2024) reports the work is available in complementary French and Italian translations: French books I–II plus part of III and excerpts from other books; Italian books III–VII. No comprehensive critical edition is available. A Geʽez–Amharic edition is discussed with scholarly cautions. A 2024 English print edition is bibliographically listed as The Book of Clement from the Ethiopian Bible, by Breandan Lumpkin (Fifth Estate, ISBN 978-1958450154). The Ethiopian Orthodox Bible Project calls it an English translation of Ethiopic Clement. Neither source establishes its exact Geʽez base, scope, completeness, translation method, accuracy, or equivalence with Maṣḥafa Qalemǝnṭos (CAe 1957); this is an unreviewed edition lead, not bundled coverage. A 2024 English print edition is bibliographically listed as The Book of Clement from the Ethiopian Bible, by Breandan Lumpkin (Fifth Estate, ISBN 978-1958450154). The Ethiopian Orthodox Bible Project calls it an English translation of Ethiopic Clement. Separately, the publisher describes a forthcoming revised reader edition with twelve modern chapters; its article says full Books V–VII lie outside that announced edition. Do not transfer this scope description to the distinct 2024 print edition. Neither edition has been inspected here for its exact Geʽez base, complete contents, translation method, accuracy, or equivalence with Maṣḥafa Qalemǝnṭos (CAe 1957). These are unbundled leads, not coverage.
Catalogue chapter note: Seven internal books reported; chapter/section boundaries not audited
Text availability: Bausi (2024) reports complementary translations covering the work, but this archive bundles no Qalemǝnṭos text. Exact editions, translation rights, and text accuracy have not been reviewed. A 2024 English print edition is identified in retailer and secondary-project metadata (SRC-381; SRC-382). The book text was not inspected or bundled; identity, boundaries, completeness, translation method, accuracy, and reuse rights remain unverified. A 2024 English print edition and a separately announced forthcoming revised reader edition are identified in retailer, secondary-project, and publisher metadata (SRC-381–SRC-383). The 2026 publisher article describes the announced edition as partial, with complete Books V–VII outside its scope; do not assume that this applies to the distinct 2024 edition. Neither book text was inspected or bundled; identity, boundaries, completeness, translation method, accuracy, publication status, and reuse rights remain unverified.
Completeness: Not assessed for any single witness or translation; do not infer completeness from seven-book descriptions
Rights note: The Bausi 2024 scholarly chapter is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; that license does not cover the manuscript or Qalemǝnṭos text. Rights for manuscripts and prior French, Italian, and Geʽez–Amharic editions require separate review. The English print listing grants no redistribution permission; rights for the edition and underlying text were not established. No text is bundled.
